questions.q: What is the real convention for deciding what goes inside a single Update Set?
options: Batch by day or by calendar schedule
Batch by feature or user story, so everything needed for one coherent piece of functionality travels together
Batch by developer, so each person has exactly one Update Set
Never batch anything — one change per Update Set always
questions.explain: Feature-based batching keeps an Update Set mapped to a real unit of business value, not an arbitrary time period or person.

questions.q: Why is splitting every tiny change into its own separate Update Set risky at scale?
options: ServiceNow does not track or enforce the dependency ordering between separate Update Sets, so promoting them in the wrong sequence can cause preview errors or silent breakage
Tiny Update Sets are not allowed by the platform
It makes each individual Update Set too large to complete
It has no real downside compared to feature-sized batching
questions.explain: With forty tiny, interdependent Update Sets, someone has to manually solve the dependency-ordering puzzle correctly every time, with no safety net.

questions.q: What is the real cost of batching several unrelated features into one broad Update Set?
options: The Update Set becomes too small to be useful
If just one of those features turns out to have a bug, you cannot roll back only that feature without also rolling back the others welded into the same set
ServiceNow will refuse to let you complete an Update Set with multiple features
There is no real cost as long as all the features eventually work
questions.explain: Partial rollback becomes impossible once unrelated features share a single Update Set — you either roll back everything or leave the bug in place.

questions.q: Before marking an Update Set complete, what two questions should you ask to check it's sized correctly?
options: Did I create it on a Tuesday, and is it the only one I made this week?
Does everything in it serve one coherent feature, and could it be promoted alone without needing another open Update Set?
Is my name on it, and is it under 10 records?
Is it the biggest Update Set I've ever made, and did I finish it fast?
questions.explain: Those two questions directly test whether the batching is feature-coherent and self-contained, the two properties correct sizing depends on.

questions.q: What did course 3's coverage of Update Sets already teach, which this lesson deliberately does not repeat?
options: How to decide what belongs together in a batch
The basic mechanics: creating an Update Set, making changes, marking it complete, and moving it between instances
How to resolve a collision between a local and remote update
How to investigate a partial commit failure
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly builds on course 3's intro-level mechanics rather than re-teaching them, focusing instead on real batching strategy.
